title: Continuous Pursuit and the Effective Date of a Grant in Decision Reviews and Appeals
content:
# Memorandum: continuous pursuit of a claim through Decision Reviews and Appeals

## Rule

When a claimant files the next review lane on an issue within the continuous pursuit period after the earlier review decision, the chain of reviews is continuous and any grant is effective as of the original claim's date of claim; a chain broken by a late filing keeps only the date of the new supplemental claim. Each request in a chain cites the review it continues.

The continuous pursuit period is 365 calendar days after the earlier review decision, the same in all six lanes of Decision Reviews and Appeals, and in every lane continuous pursuit preserves the effective date of the original claim.

## Elements of the rule

1. **The clock.** The period runs from the earlier review decision on the issue — the decision date of the review that the new request continues.
2. **The filing.** What must fall within the period is the filing of the next review lane on the same issue.
3. **The consequence of continuity.** A grant at any point in a continuous chain is effective as of the date of claim of the original claim, not the date of the later request.
4. **The consequence of a break.** Where the next filing is late, the chain is broken, and the new supplemental claim keeps only its own date.
5. **The record of the chain.** Each request in a chain cites the earlier review it continues, so the chain can be traced on the claimant's review records from the latest request back to the original claim.

## Illustrations (all dates hypothetical, stated as day counts)

| Hypothetical sequence | Next lane filed | Days after the earlier review decision | Chain | Effective date of any grant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original claim; Higher-Level Review decided adversely | Supplemental Claim | 200 | Continuous | The original claim's date of claim |
| Original claim; Supplemental Claim decided adversely | Board Appeal - Direct Review Docket | 90 | Continuous | The original claim's date of claim |
| Original claim; Higher-Level Review decided adversely | Supplemental Claim | 400 | Broken by a late filing | Only the date of the new supplemental claim |

In the first row, 200 days is within the period of 365 calendar days, so a grant on the supplemental claim reaches back to the date of claim of the original claim. In the third row, 400 days is beyond the period, so the new supplemental claim keeps only its own date.

## Questions on the memorandum

**From what point is the period counted?** From the earlier review decision that the new request continues, not from the original claim.

**Does the chain carry its date across lanes?** Yes. The rule speaks of filing the next review lane on the issue; a chain may pass from one lane to another and remain continuous so long as each next lane is filed within the period after the earlier review decision.
